messages:
sophie: quick heads up — uploaded an Nsight capture from the 8-GPU run where tail latency jumped after switching kernel selector to prefer bandwidth. link: https://internal.nsight/2140056789 :eyes:
ben: grabbing it now. what batch size / microbatch config did you use?
ajay: FYI nvprof + our timers show a weird pattern: allreduce spikes align with KV cache flush windows. sample snippet:
```
# from runtime timers
step  :  total 12.1ms  compute 6.9ms  comm 5.2ms  comm_ratio=43%
allreduce: mean=1.9ms p95=5.8ms p99=8.6ms  (many small 0.2-0.6KB transfers)
KV flush: 4 events per step, avg 0.9ms each
```
ben: small transfers over NVLink are insanely inefficient — packetization/frag adds overhead. does the capture show many concurrent small P2P ops?
sophie: yes — timeline shows many tiny DMA bursts instead of one big transfer. SM utilization drops between bursts. Nsight timeline: SM active ~74%, PCIe/NVLink xfer ~14% but in tiny bursts, idle ~12%.
maria: this sounds like fragmentation from batch-steering + KV updates not coalesced. when kernel selector switched to high-bandwidth kernels we reduced per-microbatch latency but increased number of KV ops per step, so we now have more frequent small P2P transfers.
ajay: also saw more allreduce tail when tensor-parallel ranks finish compute at slightly different times — ripple effect. comm/compute overlap falls apart with misaligned microbatches.
ben: mitigation ideas: 1) coalesce KV cache updates into a single per-step transfer (or prefix/flush spacing), 2) increase max_fragment_bytes so batch-steering groups microbatches, 3) add jitter to launch times?
maria: + add on-the-fly combiner in runtime: buffer successive KV writes for up-to N tokens or M microbatches before issuing P2P. cheap and should reduce small-transfer count.
sophie: I can test buffering but worried about latency SLO. maybe adaptive: if latency slack > X, coalesce.
ajay: wrote a quick patch to timers to measure per-transfer size + queue depth. running it now on a noisy node. output looks like:
```
transfer_samples: [512B, 1KB, 2KB, 128B, 4KB, ...]
queue_depth: mean=3 p95=7
allreduce_overlap: mean=0.18 (fraction of comm overlapped with compute)
```
infra-bot: deploy started: runtime/kv-coalesce-experiment -> canary (3 hosts). logs: https://internal.ci/2140056795
ben: good. also check NVLink lane utilization per-pair — if one link is saturated fragmentation gets worse. Nsight has per-link counters.
maria: agree. we should also compare with setting kernel_selector.prefer_high_bw=false to see if compute kernels that produce larger contiguous KV writes are overall better. tradeoffs between compute efficiency and comm granularity.
sophie: action items:
- ajay: run the coalesce timer run on 4 more configs and post aggregated numbers by EOD (2140058123)
- ben: pull per-link NVLink counters from Nsight capture and post heatmap
- maria: prototype adaptive coalescer (config knobs: max_bytes, max_microbatches, latency_slack_threshold)
- sophie: schedule another full 8-GPU capture with debug knobs (kv_coalesce=on/off, kernel_selector flag)

sophie: thanks all — this feels like a plausible root cause for the regression in parallel efficiency. tagging @platform leads if we need an infra-level tweak. :thumbsup:
